pages.text: In the tall pine at the meadow's edge, a Raven was teaching her chick to fly.
"Fly smooth and straight, little one," she said. "Like this!" And off she flew — but halfway across the sky, she wobbled left to peek at something shiny.
The chick flew smooth and straight... then wobbled left, exactly the same.
"Hm," said Raven. "Fly calm and quiet, little one. Like this!" And off she flew — but a squirrel startled her, and she let out a great loud SQUAWK.
The chick flew calm and quiet... then let out a great loud SQUAWK, exactly the same.
Raven landed on the branch and looked at her chick for a long moment. The chick looked back with round, waiting eyes.
"Little one," she said slowly, "you fly the way I fly, don't you?" "Of course," said the chick. "You're my mama. Your wings show me how."
So the next morning, Raven flew the way she hoped her chick would fly — smooth when she could, calm when she could, and honest about her wobbles.
And the chick wobbled less too. Funny how that works.
Little wings learn from watching, not from listening.
Y colorín colorado, este cuento se ha acabado.
